title: Management of the National Funds Act
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS <Amended 2011.4.4>

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to prescribe matters necessary for the management of national funds so that national funds are managed efficiently and transparently.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act mean the following:
1. “National funds” means the following assets:
(a) All cash paid into the State's revenues under statutes or regulations, contracts, etc., or into funds (meaning funds under Article 3(1)2; hereinafter the same applies), and assets prescribed by Presidential Decree as having the same value as cash (hereinafter referred to as “cash, etc.”);
(b) Cash, etc. temporarily held pending payment, as local revenues under Article 71 of the Local Tax Act, of local consumption tax collected by the State under Article 68 of that Act;
(c) Cash, etc. raised under Article 32;
(d) Financial assets acquired for the purpose of investing national funds under Article 34;
2. “Receipt” means the payment into revenues or into a fund of national funds under subparagraph 1(a), such as taxes;
3. “Disbursement” means the payment of cash, etc. from the National Treasury in execution of the expenditure budget and a fund management plan under the National Finance Act (hereinafter referred to as a “fund management plan”);
4. “Head of a central government agency” means the head of a central government agency under Article 6 of the National Finance Act.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 3 (Scope of Application)
(1) This Act applies to the following accounts or funds:
1. The general account and special accounts under Article 4 of the National Finance Act;
2. Funds managed and operated by the head of a central government agency (including cases in which fund management or operation is entrusted), among the funds established under Article 5(1) of the National Finance Act: Provided, That funds prescribed by Presidential Decree as being considered unsuitable for management as national funds in light of their public nature, purposes of establishment, methods of financing, etc. are excluded.
(2) Articles 7, 18, 28 and 30 through 33 do not apply to funds: Provided, That Article 31 applies to the Public Capital Management Fund under Article 2 of the Public Capital Management Fund Act.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 4 (Principles for Managing National Funds) National funds shall be managed to satisfy the following requirements:
1. They shall be managed efficiently and transparently in accordance with plans;
2. They shall be disbursed at the appropriate time;
3. They shall be invested within a range that does not impair their safety;
4. Matters concerning receipts, disbursements, etc. of national funds shall be recorded and managed promptly and accurately.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 4-2 (Deadline for Cash Transactions and Attribution to Fiscal Years)
(1) Affairs concerning the receipt and payment of revenues and expenditures attributable to a fiscal year shall be completed by February 10 of the following year.
(2) The attribution of revenues and expenditures to fiscal years shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 4-3 (Appointment and Duties of Cashiers)
(1) Cashiers shall be appointed by the head of each central government agency or a public official delegated by that head.
(2) Cashiers shall receive, pay and hold funds as prescribed by statutes or regulations.
(3) Appointment of cashiers under paragraph (1) may be replaced by designation of positions established in the relevant agency.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

CHAPTER II RECEIPTS <Amended 2011.4.4>

Article 5 (Principles for Collection and Acceptance of Receipts) Receipts shall be collected or accepted as prescribed by statutes or regulations.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 6 (Overall Control and Management of Receipts) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall exercise overall control over affairs concerning the collection and acceptance of receipts, and the head of each central government agency shall manage such affairs concerning receipts under that agency's jurisdiction. <Amended 2008.2.29, 2025.10.1>

Article 7 (Prohibition against Direct Use of Receipts, etc.) Except as otherwise specifically provided in other Acts, the head of a central government agency shall pay receipts under that agency's jurisdiction into the National Treasury and may not use them directly.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 8 (Expenses Financed by Receipts)
(1) The head of a central government agency may disburse expenses financed by receipts under Article 53(1) of the National Finance Act within the amount of receipts secured.
(2) The head of a central government agency may appoint a revenue collection officer for expenses financed by receipts and a revenue cashier for expenses financed by receipts, for separate accounting of such expenses under paragraph (1).
(3) Provisions concerning revenue collection officers and revenue cashiers apply to the appointment and handling of affairs of revenue collection officers for expenses financed by receipts and revenue cashiers for expenses financed by receipts.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 9 (Delegation of Revenue Collection Affairs, etc.)
(1) The head of a central government agency may delegate affairs concerning the collection of receipts under that agency's jurisdiction to subordinate public officials, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Receipts may be collected only by a public official delegated affairs concerning the collection of receipts under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as a “revenue collection officer”).
(3) Delegation of collection affairs under paragraph (1) may be replaced by the head of a central government agency designating positions established in an agency under that head.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 10 (Methods of Collecting Receipts) A revenue collection officer intending to collect receipts shall investigate and determine them and notify the taxpayer or other debtor (hereinafter referred to as a “taxpayer, etc.”) to make payment: Provided, That where a taxpayer, etc. has paid without a payment notice under statutes or regulations, contracts, etc., the revenue collection officer shall investigate and determine the receipts but may omit the payment notice.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 11 (Electronic Service of Payment Notices)
(1) Upon application by a taxpayer, etc., a revenue collection officer may serve a payment notice through an information and communications network (hereinafter referred to as “electronic service”).
(2) The Minister of Finance and Economy may have financial companies, etc. prescribed by Presidential Decree perform electronic service under paragraph (1) on the Minister's behalf. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(3) A taxpayer, etc. wishing to receive electronic service of a payment notice shall apply to a financial company, etc. performing electronic service under paragraph (2) (hereinafter referred to as an “electronic service agency”).
(4) Where a person wishing to perform electronic service on behalf of the Minister equips itself with the necessary facilities and applies for designation as an electronic service agency, the Minister of Finance and Economy shall designate it as such. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(5) The Minister of Finance and Economy may revoke designation where a designated electronic service agency violates this Act or an order under this Act, or where the Minister considers it inappropriate for the agency to continue performing electronic service for a reason prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Finance and Economy. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(6) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall hold a hearing before revoking designation of an electronic service agency under paragraph (5). <Amended 2025.10.1>
(7) The Government may pay electronic service agencies the costs necessary to receive applications for electronic service of payment notices, perform electronic service and handle other electronic service affairs, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(8) Matters necessary for electronic service of payment notices shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 12 (Receiving Institutions)
(1) Receipts may be accepted only by the cashier responsible for accepting them (hereinafter referred to as a “revenue cashier”): Provided, That this does not apply where receipt affairs are handled by the Bank of Korea under the Bank of Korea Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Bank of Korea”) or a treasury bank (meaning, where the head of a central government agency has a financial company, etc. prescribed by Presidential Decree handle cash transactions for a special account under Article 3 of the Government Enterprise Budget Act or a fund, that institution; hereinafter the same applies).
(2) Where a revenue cashier accepts receipts under paragraph (1), the cashier shall pay them into the Bank of Korea or a treasury bank without delay.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 13 (Separation of Collection and Receiving Institutions) A revenue collection officer may not concurrently perform the duties of a revenue cashier: Provided, That concurrent performance is permitted where a special reason prescribed by Presidential Decree exists.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 14 (Receipts for Previous Years) Receipts attributable to a year for which cash transactions have been closed shall all be included in the receipts of the current year.

Article 15 (Return of Erroneous Payments and Overpayments)
(1) Erroneously paid or overpaid receipts shall be returned as prescribed by Presidential Decree, irrespective of the expenditure budget or fund management plan. <Amended 2020.6.9>
(2) Where erroneously paid or overpaid receipts must be returned under paragraph (1), interest shall be paid as prescribed by Presidential Decree: Provided, That where another Act specifically provides for interest on such receipts, that Act applies.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 16 (Refund of Receipts) Where any amount paid as receipts must be refunded under an Act, it shall be refunded as prescribed by Presidential Decree, irrespective of the expenditure budget or fund management plan. <Amended 2020.6.9>
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 16-2 (Payment of Local Consumption Tax Collected by the State) Where local consumption tax collected by the State under Article 68 of the Local Tax Act is paid into local revenues under Article 71 of that Act, payment shall be made as prescribed by Presidential Decree, irrespective of the expenditure budget.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 17 (Provision of Information on Payment Notices) The head of a central government agency shall provide the Minister of Finance and Economy, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, with information concerning payment notices that is necessary for the acceptance and management of national funds. <Amended 2025.10.1>
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 18 (Funds for Advance Use)
(1) Notwithstanding Articles 7 and 12(2), a special account under Article 3 of the Government Enterprise Budget Act may operate receipts as funds for advance use (meaning funds used before payment into the National Treasury and subsequently paid into it by substituting disbursed funds; hereinafter the same applies).
(2) The head of a central government agency may appoint an officer authorizing transactions in funds for advance use and a cashier for funds for advance use, in order to operate such funds under paragraph (1).
(3) Funds for advance use shall be deposited with and managed by financial companies, etc. prescribed by Presidential Decree (hereinafter referred to as “financial companies, etc.”).
(4) Matters necessary for operating funds for advance use shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

CHAPTER III DISBURSEMENTS <Amended 2011.4.4>

Article 19 (Overall Control and Management of Disbursements) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall exercise overall control over disbursement affairs, and the head of each central government agency shall manage commitments to disburse (meaning contracts or other acts giving rise to the disbursement of national funds; hereinafter the same applies) and disbursement affairs under that agency's jurisdiction. <Amended 2025.10.1>
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 20 (Standards for Commitments to Disburse) The head of a central government agency shall make commitments to disburse within the amounts of the budget allocated under statutes or regulations or Article 43 of the National Finance Act, or within the amounts of the fund management plan.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 21 (Delegation of Commitments to Disburse)
(1) The head of a central government agency may delegate the making of commitments to disburse to subordinate public officials, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Delegation of commitments to disburse under paragraph (1) may be replaced by the head of a central government agency designating positions established in an agency under that head.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 22 (Disbursement Procedures)
(1) Where the head of a central government agency or a public official delegated under Article 21 (hereinafter referred to as a “finance officer”) intends to disburse under the expenditure budget or fund management plan under that person's jurisdiction, the person shall forward documents concerning the commitment to disburse to a public official appointed by the head of the central government agency to which the person belongs (hereinafter referred to as a “disbursing officer”), as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Appointment of a disbursing officer may be replaced by the head of a central government agency designating positions established in an agency under that head.
(3) A disbursing officer intending to disburse pursuant to a commitment to disburse shall pay by transfer into the account of the creditor or a person entrusted under statutes or regulations with handling the payment of national funds (hereinafter referred to as a “creditor, etc.”), as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(4) Where payment under paragraph (3) is impossible because of an information and communications failure or other unavoidable reason, the disbursing officer may pay cash, etc. directly to the creditor, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(5) Disbursements under paragraphs (1), (3) and (4) shall remain within the detailed monthly cash plan for each disbursing officer under Article 30(6).
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 23 (Restrictions on Disbursements) A disbursing officer may disburse only where a creditor, etc. is the payee: Provided, That this does not apply to the delivery of funds to a cashier.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 24 (Payment of Office Operating Expenses)
(1) For expenses necessary to operate an agency whose nature makes disbursement under Article 22 liable to impede the performance of duties (hereinafter referred to as “office operating expenses”), the head of a central government agency or a public official delegated by that head may have a cashier obtain the necessary funds from the disbursing officer and make payment.
(2) A cashier receiving and paying office operating expenses under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as an “office operating expense cashier”) may make commitments to pay within the funds delivered under paragraph (1), as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) Office operating expenses may be paid only by an office operating expense cashier.
(4) Office operating expense cashiers shall deposit office operating expenses with financial companies, etc. for management.
(5) An office operating expense cashier intending to pay office operating expenses shall use a government purchase card (meaning a credit card or debit card under Article 2, subparagraphs 3 and 6, of the Specialized Credit Finance Business Act, or an electronic debit payment means under Article 2, subparagraph 13, of the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, used to pay office operating expenses as prescribed by Presidential Decree; hereinafter the same applies): Provided, That where the nature of the expense precludes use of a government purchase card, payment may be made in cash or by another method prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2016.12.27>
(6) Matters necessary for the scope of office operating expenses, payment procedures, methods of using government purchase cards, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 25 (Delivery of Office Operating Expenses before the Start of a Fiscal Year)
(1) Only in the case of office operating expenses, the head of a central government agency or a public official delegated by that head may have an office operating expense cashier obtain necessary funds from the disbursing officer and make payment before the fiscal year begins.
(2) The Minister of Finance and Economy may temporarily borrow funds to be delivered before the fiscal year begins under paragraph (1), within the maximum amount of temporary borrowings for that fiscal year. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(3) Matters necessary for the delivery of office operating expenses before the fiscal year begins shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 26 (Advance Payments and Payments on an Estimated Basis) A disbursing officer may make advance payments or payments on an estimated basis for freight charges, vessel charter hire, consideration under construction, manufacturing or service contracts, and other expenses prescribed by Presidential Decree whose nature makes failure to pay in advance or on an estimated basis liable to impede the relevant affairs or project.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 27 (Separation of Disbursing Institutions and Cash Handling Institutions) The duties of finance officer, disbursing officer and cashier may not be performed concurrently: Provided, That for a fund, the duties of disbursing officer and cashier may be performed concurrently as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 28 (Disbursements for Previous Years) Expenses consisting of established debts attributable to a previous year that remain unpaid shall be disbursed from the current year's expenditure budget, but may not exceed the unused amount of the relevant budget item for the year to which those expenses belong: Provided, That expenses recognized by Presidential Decree as unavoidably requiring disbursement because of their nature are excepted.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 29 (Return of Disbursed Funds)
(1) Where disbursed amounts are returned, they shall be returned to the respective items from which they were disbursed, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), returned disbursements attributable to a year for which cash transactions have been closed shall be included in the current year's receipts.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

CHAPTER IV CASH MANAGEMENT

Article 30 (Cash Plans)
(1) Upon establishment of the budget, the head of a central government agency shall prepare and submit to the Minister of Finance and Economy a monthly cash plan comprehensively considering receipt and disbursement forecasts and other matters concerning cash transactions. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(2) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall compile the plans under paragraph (1) and prepare a monthly cash plan. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(3) The head of a central government agency shall prepare and submit a detailed monthly cash plan to the Minister of Finance and Economy each month, in accordance with the monthly cash plan prepared under paragraph (2). <Amended 2025.10.1>
(4) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall compile the detailed monthly cash plans submitted by the heads of central government agencies under paragraph (3), prepare a detailed monthly cash plan, and notify those heads and the Bank of Korea thereof. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(5) Where necessary for the supply of and demand for cash, the Minister of Finance and Economy may adjust the detailed monthly cash plan under paragraph (4). In such cases, the Minister of Finance and Economy shall notify the head of the relevant central government agency and the Bank of Korea. <Amended 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>
(6) Upon receiving notice of a detailed monthly cash plan under paragraphs (4) and (5), the head of a central government agency shall notify each subordinate disbursing officer of the detailed monthly cash plan for that officer.
(7) Matters necessary for preparation and adjustment of the cash plans under paragraphs (1) through (6) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 31 (Integrated Management of National Funds, etc.)
(1) Where necessary for transactions in national funds, the Minister of Finance and Economy may manage on an integrated basis, outside the revenue and expenditure budget, the cash of accounts or subaccounts prescribed by Presidential Decree among the Government's various accounts or subaccounts (including amounts carried over from the previous year and surplus revenues). In such cases, national funds disbursed from the integrated account in connection with expenditures of an individual account or subaccount during the relevant fiscal year may not exceed national funds received in the integrated account in connection with revenues of that individual account. <Amended 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>
(2) An integrated account shall be established at the Bank of Korea for integrated management of national funds under paragraph (1).
(3) Where necessary for the supply of and demand for national funds, the Minister of Finance and Economy may arrange mutual deposits of cash among accounts or subaccounts not subject to integrated management under paragraph (1), the integrated account under paragraph (2) (hereinafter referred to as the “integrated account”) and the Public Capital Management Fund under Article 2 of the Public Capital Management Fund Act, outside the revenue and expenditure budget or fund management plan, to the extent that execution of the budget or fund management plan is not impeded. In such cases, the deposits shall be repaid from revenues of the relevant fiscal year. <Amended 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>
(4) Matters necessary for integrated management or mutual deposits under paragraph (1) or (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 32 (Raising Cash)
(1) Where necessary for transactions in national funds, the State may raise cash by issuing treasury bills under Article 33, by temporary borrowing from the Bank of Korea, or by other methods prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2020.6.9>
(2) Cash raised under paragraph (1) shall be repaid from revenues of the relevant fiscal year.
(3) The maximum cash to be raised under paragraph (1) shall be approved by resolution of the National Assembly for each fiscal year for each account or subaccount requiring cash (excluding accounts or subaccounts included in the integrated account; hereinafter the same applies in paragraph (4)), the integrated account and each fund. <Amended 2020.6.9>
(4) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall raise cash under paragraph (1) at the expense of the respective accounts or subaccounts requiring cash, the integrated account and funds: Provided, That the costs of raising cash for, and interest payable by, the integrated account shall first be covered from income under Article 34(2), and the general account shall bear any shortfall. <Amended 2020.6.9, 2025.10.1>
(5) When raising cash under paragraphs (1) and (4), the Minister of Finance and Economy shall give priority to raising cash by issuing treasury bills under Article 33. <Newly inserted 2016.12.27, 2025.10.1>
(6) Cash temporarily borrowed from the Bank of Korea under paragraph (1) shall be repaid without delay when the need for the cash ceases. <Newly inserted 2016.12.27, 2020.6.9>
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 33 (Issuance of Treasury Bills, etc.)
(1) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall issue treasury bills at the expense of the general account or a special account (limited to one permitted by an Act to borrow temporarily). <Amended 2025.10.1>
(2) Treasury bills shall be issued on the open market: Provided, That where necessary, they may be sold to financial companies, etc., government-invested enterprises, insurance companies or other persons.
(3) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall determine and publicly announce matters necessary for treasury bills, including their interest rates, maturity dates and redemption conditions. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(4) Treasury bills issued under paragraph (1) shall be electronically registered in registered or bearer form in the treasury bill register using a computerized information processing system, without issuing certificates: Provided, That certificates in registered or bearer form may be issued in time of war, armed conflict or a comparable national emergency, etc. <Amended 2016.3.2>
(5) Transfer of treasury bills or creation of a pledge over them may not be asserted against the Government or any other third party unless the fact is registered. <Amended 2016.3.2>
(6) Treasury bills shall be issued at face value or at a discount.
(7) Claims under treasury bills are extinguished by prescription if not exercised for five years from the day after their maturity date.
(8) Matters necessary for issuing and redeeming treasury bills shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(9) The Bank of Korea shall perform the registration affairs under paragraphs (4) and (5). <Newly inserted 2016.3.2>
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 34 (Investment of National Funds)
(1) Where the Minister of Finance and Economy considers that transactions in national funds will not be impeded, the Minister may invest cash in the integrated account outside the revenue and expenditure budget by any of the following methods: <Amended 2025.10.1>
1. Buying or selling government bonds, public bonds and monetary stabilization bonds issued under the Bank of Korea Monetary Stabilization Bond Act;
2. Depositing with or lending on a short-term basis to financial companies, etc. prescribed by Presidential Decree;
3. Buying or selling debt certificates issued by securities finance companies or merchant banks under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act;
4. Buying or selling other securities prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) The Minister of Finance and Economy may use income from investment of cash in the integrated account under paragraph (1), outside the revenue and expenditure budget, for the following purposes: <Amended 2025.10.1>
1. Paying the costs of raising cash and interest for the integrated account under the proviso to Article 32(4);
2. Paying other expenses related to investment of national funds.
(3) The head of a central government agency managing an account or subaccount not included in the integrated account may invest national funds of the account or subaccount under that agency's jurisdiction in accordance with paragraphs (1) and (2).
(4) The head of a central government agency may invest surplus cash of funds under that agency's jurisdiction outside the fund management plan, by methods prescribed by relevant statutes or regulations.
(5) Income from investment of national funds under paragraphs (1), (3) and (4) shall accrue to the integrated account, respective accounts or subaccounts, or funds making the investment.
(6) A national funds investment account shall be established at the Bank of Korea for accounting for investment of national funds in the integrated account.
(7) Matters necessary for investment of national funds shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(8) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall report annually to the National Assembly on investment of national funds in the integrated account. <Amended 2025.10.1>
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS <Amended 2011.4.4>

Article 35 (Restrictions on Holding Cash) The head of a central government agency may not hold national funds in cash except as provided by statutes or regulations.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 36 (Cash Transactions in National Funds by the Bank of Korea, etc.)
(1) The Bank of Korea and treasury banks (hereinafter referred to as the “Bank of Korea, etc.”) shall handle transactions in national funds as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) The Bank of Korea, etc. may have financial companies, etc. handle transactions in national funds on their behalf, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Finance and Economy. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(3) National funds received by the Bank of Korea, etc. under paragraph (1) shall constitute State deposits as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(4) The Bank of Korea, etc. shall submit to examination by the Board of Audit and Inspection concerning the transactions in national funds they handle.
(5) The Civil Act and Commercial Act apply to liability for compensation where the Bank of Korea, etc. or financial companies, etc. acting on their behalf under paragraph (2) cause loss to the State in connection with the receipt, payment or custody of national funds.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 37 (Records of National Funds Management Affairs) Revenue collection officers, finance officers, disbursing officers, officers authorizing transactions in funds for advance use under Article 18(2), cashiers, other public officials engaged in accounting prescribed by Presidential Decree, and the Bank of Korea, etc. shall maintain books and record matters necessary for managing national funds, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 38 (Submission of Reports and Statements of Accounts)
(1) The head of a central government agency shall prepare and submit reports on national funds management to the Minister of Finance and Economy, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(2) Revenue collection officers, finance officers, disbursing officers, officers authorizing transactions in funds for advance use, cashiers, other public officials engaged in accounting prescribed by Presidential Decree, and the Bank of Korea, etc. shall prepare reports on national funds management and submit them to the head of the central government agency, the Minister of Finance and Economy and the Board of Audit and Inspection, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(3) Cashiers and the Bank of Korea, etc. shall report to the revenue collection officer or disbursing officer on the receipts or disbursed funds they have handled, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(4) Revenue collection officers, finance officers, disbursing officers, officers authorizing transactions in funds for advance use and cashiers shall prepare statements of accounts concerning national funds management as prescribed by the Board of Audit and Inspection, and submit them to the head of the central government agency, the Minister of Finance and Economy and the Board of Audit and Inspection. <Amended 2025.10.1>
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 39 (Consultation on Statutes and Regulations concerning National Funds Management) When drafting statutes or regulations concerning national funds management, the head of a central government agency shall consult the Minister of Finance and Economy. <Amended 2025.10.1>
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 40 (Acting and Divided-Duty Public Officials Engaged in Accounting)
(1) Where necessary, the head of a central government agency may have a subordinate public official act for a revenue collection officer or finance officer in all of that officer's affairs, or separately undertake part of them, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Where necessary, the head of a central government agency or a public official delegated by that head may appoint a public official to act for a disbursing officer, an officer authorizing transactions in funds for advance use or a cashier in all of that officer's affairs, or separately undertake part of them, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) Acting and divided-duty assignments for the affairs of a revenue collection officer, finance officer, disbursing officer, officer authorizing transactions in funds for advance use or cashier under paragraphs (1) and (2) may be replaced by the head of a central government agency designating positions established in an agency under that head.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 41 (Special Cases concerning Appointment of Public Officials Engaged in Accounting)
(1) Where necessary, the head of a central government agency may delegate revenue collection officer or finance officer affairs to a public official of another central government agency, or appoint such a public official as a disbursing officer or cashier, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Delegation of revenue collection officer or finance officer affairs, or appointment of a disbursing officer or cashier, under paragraph (1) may be replaced by the head of a central government agency designating positions established in another central government agency.
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 42 (Handling of National Funds Management Affairs by Local Governments, etc.)
(1) The State may have public officials of local governments, or executives or employees of public institutions under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions (hereinafter referred to as “public institutions”) or financial companies, etc., handle national funds management affairs, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Provisions of this Act or other statutes or regulations concerning national funds management that govern the handling of such affairs apply mutatis mutandis to public officials of local governments and executives or employees of public institutions or financial companies, etc. handling such affairs under paragraph (1).
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 43 (Delegation of Disbursement Affairs)
(1) The head of a central government agency may delegate disbursement affairs under that agency's jurisdiction to public officials of another agency, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) The Minister of Finance and Economy shall appoint the public officials engaged in accounting who will execute affairs delegated under paragraph (1), as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2025.10.1>
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 44 (Entrustment of Affairs concerning Treasury Bills, etc.) The Minister of Finance and Economy may entrust to the Governor of the Bank of Korea affairs concerning the issuance and redemption of treasury bills under Article 33 and part of the affairs concerning investment of national funds under Article 34. <Amended 2025.10.1>
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 45 (Fidelity Guarantees for Public Officials Engaged in Accounting)
(1) Revenue collection officers, finance officers, disbursing officers, officers authorizing transactions in funds for advance use, cashiers and other public officials engaged in accounting prescribed by Presidential Decree may not perform their duties without a fidelity guarantee prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) The State shall bear expenses related to fidelity guarantees under paragraph (1).
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 46 (Informatization of Business Processing)
(1) Where necessary for the smooth performance of national funds management affairs under this Act, the Minister of Finance and Economy may develop information and communications media, programs, etc. and have the heads of central government agencies use them, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2025.10.1>
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the head of a central government agency may develop and use information and communications media, programs, etc. for handling national funds management affairs under this Act. In such cases, the head shall first consult the Minister of Finance and Economy and the Board of Audit and Inspection. <Amended 2025.10.1>
[Wholly amended 2011.4.4]

Article 47 (Rounding of National Funds)
(1) For receipts or disbursements of national funds, a fractional amount of less than 10 won shall be disregarded; where the entire amount is less than 10 won, the entire amount shall also be disregarded: Provided, That this does not apply in cases prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) In calculating the assessment base for national taxes, a fractional amount of less than 1 won shall be disregarded.

1. The amended provisions in the following items enter into force on 2026.1.2: Provided, That among the Acts amended under Article 7 of the Addenda (limited to portions related to the amended provisions in items (a) and (b)), amendments to Acts promulgated before the enforcement date under the main clause but whose enforcement dates have not yet arrived by that date enter into force on the respective enforcement dates of those Acts.

(a) The amended provisions of Article 19(4), Article 23, Article 29(1)1 and Article 30;

(b) The amended provisions of Article 12(2), Article 19(3), Article 22 and the proviso to Article 29(2) (limited to portions concerning the Minister of Finance and Economy and the Ministry of Finance and Economy);

(c) Acts amended under Article 7 of the Addenda (limited to portions related to the amended provisions in items (a) and (b)).

2. Omitted.

Articles 2 through 6 Omitted.

Article 7 (Amendments to Other Acts) (1) through (14) Omitted.

(15) The Management of the National Funds Act is amended as follows.

In Article 6; Article 11(2) and (4) through (6); Articles 17 and 19; Article 25(2); Article 30(1) through (4) and the former and latter parts of paragraph (5) of that Article; the former parts of Article 31(1) and (3); the main clause of Article 32(4) and paragraph (5) of that Article; Article 33(1) and (3); the portion of Article 34(1) preceding its subparagraphs, the portion of paragraph (2) of that Article preceding its subparagraphs, and paragraph (8) of that Article; Article 38(1), (2) and (4); Article 39; Article 43(2); Article 44; Article 46(1); and the latter part of paragraph (2) of that Article, “Minister of Economy and Finance” is each replaced by “Minister of Finance and Economy”.

In Article 11(5) and Article 36(2), “Ordinance of the Ministry of Economy and Finance” is each replaced by “Ordinance of the Ministry of Finance and Economy”.

(16) through (626) Omitted.

Article 8 Omitted.
